subject: Hyperion platform disruption: corrective plan, timelines, exec sync
messages:
From: Luca Marino <luca@hyperionretail.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hyperion Retail Support <ops@hyperionretail.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Spike in errors & latency impacting checkout (we need urgent help)

Mina —

We started seeing a large spike across our checkout microservices at ~07:40 PST. Symptoms: error rate jumped to ~28% for inference calls, P95 latency increased from ~320ms to ~2.3s, and throughput dropped as clients started retrying. This is causing failed checkouts and high customer impact.

Attached are the trace samples and a short CSV of error clusters. We’ve paused a subset of traffic as a stopgap but need a plan to get to stable and prevent recurrence. Can you get us a timeline for (1) immediate containment, (2) root cause, (3) corrective actions? Our execs are watching.

Thanks,
Luca
Director, Platform Ops
Hyperion Retail

[Attachment: hyperion_latency_trace.zip (1.2MB)]

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Luca Marino <luca@hyperionretail.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 08:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in errors & latency impacting checkout (we need urgent help)

Luca — thanks for the signal and the traces. I’m pulling engineering and SRE in now. Immediate plan:

- Triage bridge (15 min) — joining link in separate calendar invite.
- Short-term containment — route traffic to the last-known-good model variant and enable conservative batching knobs (will reduce cost but restore p95).
- Collect KV cache dumps and full request traces (Ben, can you grab the traces Luca attached + the serving node metrics?).

Grace, Ben — please prioritize. Luca, we’ll confirm containment actions and an ETA for an RCA readout within 24 hours.

Mina Haddad
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.ai

--- Original attachment referenced by Luca ---

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 08:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in errors & latency impacting checkout (we need urgent help)

Joining bridge now. Quick notes from initial triage:

- Observed a surge in concurrent connections to a small subset of shards hosting the Hyperion model variant v3.1. KV cache hit dropped sharply (from 82% to ~12%).
- Memory pressure on those pods led to GC thrash and retried requests — explains both latency and error spikes.
- Rolling traffic to v3.0 (compatible variant, slightly older) stabilizes p95 within ~10 minutes in our staging repro.

Attachments I’m uploading: serving-node-metrics-0700-0900.csv and a short flamegraph.

Immediate action taken:
- Activated failover to v3.0 for Hyperion prod traffic (traffic ramp-down 30 min).
- Enabled KV cache warming for key prefixes used by checkout.

Next: full RCA and action list by tomorrow 14:00 PST.

Ben
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: serving-node-metrics-0700-0900.csv]

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Luca Marino <luca@hyperionretail.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Interim summary & governance ask — Hyperion incident

Luca / team — quick interim summary following the bridge:

What happened (summary):
- A traffic pattern change during a partner campaign caused an unexpected hot key distribution for Hyperion v3.1. The serving layer saw cache misses and pod-level memory pressure which cascaded into GC-induced latency and elevated 5xxs.

Containment status:
- Traffic moved to v3.0; p95 returned to ~340ms and error rate dropped below 1.5% within 22 minutes.
- No customer data exposure observed.

Proposed governance for exec sync and follow-through:
- Exec brief tomorrow 10:00 PST (30m) — present RCA, risk matrix, timelines. Requesting Hyperion exec + Redwood leadership (I will present).
- 8-week corrective program with milestones across: serving hardening, adaptive batching, KV cache autoscaling, and model-variant rollout gating.
- Weekly checkpoint emails and a single shared tracker (we’ll populate with owners/dates).

Action items (short list):
1) Ben — produce full trace-backed RCA and HotKey fingerprint by 14:00 PST tomorrow.
2) Kim — prepare rollback/variant gating playbook and approval flow.
3) Mina — coordinate exec invite and draft the briefing note.

Luca — please confirm exec availability and if legal/regulatory needs to be looped in.

Grace O'Connor
VP, Customer Reliability

[Attachment: hyperion-action-plan-2027-06-21.xlsx]

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Luca Marino <luca@hyperionretail.com>, Hyperion Retail Support <ops@hyperionretail.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 09:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Deliverable: timeline, RCA summary, and owner commitments (Hyperion)

Team — following the exec sync this morning, attaching the deliverable bundle. Key points:

- Root cause: Hot-key distribution to v3.1 combined with insufficient serving-node headroom; cache warmup not triggered by sudden campaign traffic.
- Immediate fixes completed: automated failover to previous variant, KV cache warming changes, and conservative request throttling during rollout windows.
- 8-week corrective plan with owners and acceptance criteria attached. Highlights:
  * Week 1–2: rollout gating and variant approval flow (owner: Kimberly), automated capacity guardrails (owner: Ben).
  * Week 3–6: adaptive batching and cache autoscaling experiments (owner: Engineering + SRE).
  * Week 7–8: DR runbook, SLA addendum draft for Hyperion (owner: Mina + Customer Success).

Deliverables and checkpoints: weekly status email (Fridays), weekly syncs for the first 4 weeks, and a final compliance package including traces and perf baselines at week 8.

Links to artifacts: https://drive.redwood.ai/Hyperion/Hyperion-RCA-2027-06-22

Please review owners and acceptance criteria in the attached exec brief and the action spreadsheet. Confirm any missing items by EOD tomorrow so we can publish the tracker to Hyperion execs.

Mina Haddad
Head of Customer Reliability
[Attachment: exec-brief-2027-06-22.pdf]

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Luca Marino <luca@hyperionretail.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Jul 2027 15:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Hyperion follow-up: week 2 checkpoint and early wins

Team / Luca — brief status update as we hit the week-2 checkpoint:

Wins to date:
- Variant gating playbook (Kim) is in place and tested in staging during a controlled traffic spike — rollout approval flow reduced risky rollouts by preventing simultaneous rollout of multiple variants.
- Capacity guardrails (Ben) prevented two near-miss memory pressure events in prod during a load test.
- P95 for checkout inference stabilized to ~360ms across canary and prod. Error rate consistently <1.2%.

Open items:
- Adaptive batching experiments are mid-run; early signs show 12–18% token-cost reduction with no quality regressions. Still need an A/B test across checkout to be confident. (Owner: Engineering)
- Final SLA addendum draft pending legal review — target EOD next Wednesday. (Owner: Mina)

Action requests:
- Hyperion: continue sending campaign start times at least 48 hours in advance so we can pre-warm caches and run a canary.
- Redwood: we’ll publish the week-2 executive highlight by Friday.

Thanks all — progress looks solid; I’ll publish the tracker after incorporating Kim’s latest dates.

Mina Haddad
Head of Customer Reliability
mina_haddad@redwood.ai

[End of thread]
